incidents.victim: Indian Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE)
incidents.vector: Vulnerabilities in the OnMark online grading portal — used to upload scanned student answer books — were publicly flagged by a teenage security researcher before any confirmed exploitation.
incidents.impact: CBSE said it has been monitoring and containing the weaknesses; no confirmed data exfiltration, but the portal handles answer sheets for one of India's largest school-leaving exams, prompting student protests at CBSE headquarters.

incidents.vector: Phishing compromise of a single Carnival employee account in April 2026 gave the attackers access to a limited portion of the IT environment, from which personal data was copied.
incidents.impact: Confirmed theft of names, addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, driver's license numbers and passport numbers for nearly 6 million people across Princess, Holland America, Cunard and Costa brands; attackers previously released 8.7M records and attempted extortion.

incidents.vector: Vishing and phishing impersonating IT support to gain remote desktop access; when that fails, an associate is dispatched in person to plug a USB or external drive into the victim's workstation. Data is then exfiltrated via WinSCP or Rclone to Google Drive, OneDrive or physical media.
incidents.impact: FBI alert: more than 100 attacks since spring 2023 with a surge in early 2026; Halcyon tracked 134 ransomware incidents against law firms in Q1 2026, making legal the fourth-most-targeted sector. Group threatens to leak attorney-client materials to pressure payment.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of an unpatched vulnerability in Ajax's ticketing and stadium-ban management systems (March 2026 intrusion).
incidents.impact: Dutch police arrested a 35-year-old in Buren and seized digital storage devices; original breach exposed limited personal data of stadium-banned individuals and may have affected over 300,000 registered supporters and 42,000 season-ticket records, with potential to alter ticket transfers and ban records.

incidents.victim: Oregon state government office and other U.S. victims
incidents.vector: Unauthorized network intrusion (June 2021) into an Oregon state government computer; access then sold to other criminals along with sample personally identifiable information.
incidents.impact: Catalin Dragomir sentenced to 56 months in U.S. federal prison; sold access to numerous U.S. victim networks for at least $250,000 in losses.

incidents.vector: Automated push of 5,718 malicious commits using dummy accounts and forged author identities, injecting a malicious GitHub Actions workflow ("SysDiag" YAML) that exfiltrates CI/CD secrets, cloud credentials, SSH keys, OIDC tokens and source-code secrets to a C2 server. A secondary payload installs a dormant workflow_dispatch backdoor.
incidents.impact: 5,718 malicious commits across 5,561 repositories in a six-hour window on May 18; Tiledesk and other downstream packages unknowingly republished poisoned code. Roughly 83% of affected repos remained infected over a week later.

incidents.vector: Out-of-band patch for CVE-2026-45659, a deserialization-of-untrusted-data flaw in on-premises SharePoint that lets any authenticated user with minimum Site Member privileges run code remotely on the server.
incidents.impact: CVSS 8.8; no public exploit yet but Microsoft's decision to release the patch off-cycle signals significant concern. SharePoint has a long history of weaponization (e.g., July 2025 ToolShell zero-day chain used against government and the U.S. Nuclear Weapons Agency).

incidents.vector: Zero-day exploitation of CVE-2026-5426, an ASP.NET ViewState deserialization flaw caused by identical hardcoded machineKey values across customer deployments. Attackers crafted malicious __VIEWSTATE payloads, deployed the BLUEBEAM (Godzilla) in-memory web shell in w3wp.exe, modified application JavaScript to push a fake "security plugin" download, and ultimately infected workstations with a Cobalt Strike BEACON keyed to the victim organization.
incidents.impact: Mandiant-disclosed compromise of a Japanese LMS web server; site visitors were redirected to a fake installer leading to Cobalt Strike infection on user workstations; broad ecosystem of internet-facing KnowledgeDeliver instances using shared keys remains at risk pending key rotation.

incidents.victim: Stark Industries / MIRhosting / WorkTitans BV (Russia-aligned hosting infrastructure)
incidents.vector: Operators allegedly provided IT infrastructure used by Russian-aligned actors for DDoS attacks, influence operations and disinformation campaigns inside the EU, including operations targeting Danish municipal elections in November 2025.
incidents.impact: Dutch FIOD arrested MIRhosting founder Andrey Nesterenko (39) and Youssef Zinad (57) on May 18; raids in Enschede, Almere, Dronten and Schiphol-Rijk seized over 800 servers, laptops and phones. Hosting customers lost data with no recovery option.

incidents.victim: Aerospace, defense and technology firms in the U.S., Israel, UAE and Middle East
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing lures impersonating a global air carrier and a video conferencing platform via tailored "Hiring Portal" ZIP archives, followed by DLL sideloading and AppDomainManager hijacking to disable .NET security in legitimate apps. Six new RAT variants split between two malware families (MiniUpdate and MiniJunk V2), with C2 routed through 3-5 dedicated Azure-hosted domains per target.
incidents.impact: Unit 42-disclosed campaigns from mid-February through April 2026, timed to the regional conflict that began Feb 28, 2026. Targets include U.S., Israel, UAE and two additional Middle Eastern entities; demonstrates expanded technical capability and operational tempo.

incidents.victim: Australian Member of Parliament Zali Steggall and three staffers
incidents.vector: Compromise of WhatsApp accounts; details of the technique not disclosed publicly but consistent with broader Russian campaigns targeting Signal and WhatsApp accounts of foreign politicians.
incidents.impact: Independent MP's WhatsApp account and those of three staffers breached in March 2026; suspected to be part of a Russian campaign against foreign politicians' messaging accounts.

incidents.vector: Use of compromised credentials issued to other Lithuanian government agencies that had legitimate authorization to query the land and real-estate registry.
incidents.impact: Approximately 600,000 records exfiltrated, including real names, cadastral information and other real-estate-specific details.

incidents.vector: Not publicly disclosed; attackers claim to have stolen sensitive financial documents from MyPillow's corporate network.
incidents.impact: Play ransomware group is extorting the company; MyPillow had not publicly confirmed the incident as of reporting.

incidents.vector: A GitHub employee installed a poisoned version of the Nx Console Visual Studio Code extension. Earlier compromise of an Nx Console maintainer's GitHub credentials let the attackers publish a malicious extension version to the VS Code Marketplace, which then executed with full developer privileges on the employee's machine.
incidents.impact: Approximately 3,800 GitHub-internal repositories exfiltrated and offered for sale on a cybercrime forum (later threatened to be leaked for free). GitHub contained the incident, rotated critical secrets and assesses the compromise as limited to internal repos; up to ~6,000 developers may have installed the poisoned extension overall.

incidents.vector: Botnet recruited internet-facing devices traditionally firewalled from the broader internet — digital photo frames, web cameras — and rented access for DDoS-for-hire and direct attacks, including against U.S. Department of Defense IP ranges.
incidents.impact: Ontario Provincial Police arrested Jacob Butler (23) of Ottawa on a U.S. extradition warrant; Kimwolf issued 25,000+ attack commands and reached nearly 30 Tbps — a record DDoS volume — with some victims losing over $1M. U.S. and partners had seized Kimwolf, Aisuru, JackSkid and Mossad infrastructure on March 19.

incidents.vector: Abused Microsoft Artifact Signing to mint short-lived, fraudulent code-signing certificates for ransomware and malware affiliates, who used them to make payloads look like AnyDesk, Teams, PuTTY, Webex and other trusted software and bypass AV/EDR.
incidents.impact: Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit seized Fox Tempest's website, took down hundreds of VMs and revoked over 1,000 certificates. The service had created 1,000+ certs and hundreds of Azure tenants, generating millions in payments from ransomware affiliates; thousands of victim machines in the U.S., China, France and India were infected with malware families including Oyster, Lumma Stealer and Vidar.

incidents.victim: Multiple npm package maintainers and downstream consumers (TanStack, OpenSearch, UiPath, Mistral AI and others)
incidents.vector: Mini Shai-Hulud worm: a postinstall hook in poisoned npm packages harvests GitHub tokens, npm tokens, SSH keys, cloud credentials and DB strings, abuses CI runner OIDC tokens to publish further poisoned versions under legitimate maintainers, and installs OS-level persistence via systemd/LaunchAgent. Initial vector against TanStack chained three GitHub Actions weaknesses (pwn_request, cache poisoning, OIDC extraction from runner memory) — no stolen credential required — producing the first malicious npm packages with valid SLSA Build Level 3 provenance.
incidents.impact: 84 malicious package artifacts published across 42 @tanstack/* packages within six minutes; by end of day, 373 malicious versions across 169 npm packages plus PyPI packages affected. Worm spread to @opensearch-project/opensearch, 57 @uipath/* packages, @mistralai/mistralai and many others; @tanstack/react-router alone has 12.7M weekly downloads. Worm source code released publicly on May 12, enabling copycats. Grafana also tied a separate breach to the TanStack incident.

incidents.victim: U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
incidents.vector: A CISA contractor (Nightwing) created a public GitHub profile called "Private-CISA" and disabled GitHub's built-in secret-scanning protections, then committed plaintext credentials for AWS GovCloud and dozens of internal CISA systems — including an RSA private key with full access to all CISA-IT GitHub repositories — apparently using the repo as a personal sync between work and home.
incidents.impact: Exposed credentials publicly visible since November 2025 with the most sensitive data committed in late April 2026; researchers warn the public GitHub firehose is monitored by criminal and state actors. More than a week after notification, CISA was still rotating credentials. Senators and House Democrats are demanding briefings; comes amid major CISA workforce cuts.
